主要内容: E.l.f. Beauty (ELF) reported better-than-expected fourth-quarter results for 2020, driven by strong online sales growth. The company's digital sales rose by triple digits as consumers shifted to online shopping amid the impact of the coronavirus pandemic. Despite a loss of $300,000, or 1 cent per share, for the quarter ended March 31, adjusted earnings of 10 cents per share exceeded Wall Street analysts' expectations. E.l.f. generated nearly $75 million in sales, marking a 13% increase from the previous year. The company suspended its 2021 forecast due to ongoing economic uncertainty and the continued impact of the pandemic on consumer behavior. CEO Tarang Amin emphasized the importance of the company's online marketplace and accessible pricing strategy in driving growth. He also noted that the rebound in sales could be partly attributed to stimulus checks and the gradual reopening of the economy. E.l.f. Beauty reported stronger-than-expected results for its fourth quarter of 2020, driven by increased online sales. The company's CEO, Amin, stated that its digital strength and value proposition should allow it to recover more quickly from the coronavirus crisis compared to competitors. Despite a nearly 11% decline in shares this year, E.l.f. has seen a 46% increase since April, outperforming its main competitor, Ulta Beauty, which has advanced 26% during the same period. E.l.f. has a market value of $721 million, significantly lower than Ulta's $12.5 billion valuation. The company's performance highlights its resilience in the beauty sector amid the ongoing challenges posed by the pandemic.
